scope: Gameplay regional preparation. Same benchmark harness with dba85c8 vs worktree runtime; Node CPU and instrumented scheduled slices, not browser FPS or an input-latency guarantee.
conclusions: Both travel scenarios eliminate sampled 8.33 ms tick overruns. P99 increases because generation is distributed over more ticks.

Both measured means increase (travel about 15%, automatic combat about 2.5%). Travel terrain cache ends at 120 instead of 110 chunks because prefetch prepares a not-yet-entered adjacent window; authoritative replay remains exact.
Scheduled startup still has roughly 39?42 ms constructor/first-work slices and far teleport roughly 17?18 ms peak slices. Chunk jobs are not preemptible; total loading cost remains.
Prepared layouts remain private until the entire window is ready; movement, dash, saved-position loading, teleport and disposal have independent unit coverage.

Waiting remains in wall time.

replay.scope: Node CPU only; expiry setup and snapshot structured clone excluded; render roundtrip uses synchronous structuredClone, not browser scheduling or GPU; copy kernels do not compact the protocol.

verification.expandedBrowserRun: Interrupted after 1 pass and 3 timeouts in mouse input, unpaused session quiescence and screenshot capture. Quiescence test updated to pause first; visual suite not accepted as passing.
verification.concurrentUnitAttempt: 9 timeouts while software-rendered browser suite competed for CPU; standalone full run passed all 489 tests.
verification.developmentServer: Fresh Vite server on port 5173; check:app:dev passed real unbundled Worker pickup, sampled minimap, skill dragging and shader checks.
verification.homeRetest: Failed before reaching the adjusted quiescence barrier: selecting wilderness left the preview label at homestead for 20 seconds. No application exception in the trace; GPU ReadPixels stall warnings occurred. This expanded UI flow remains unresolved, not counted as passed.

followUpAudit.scope: Failure and timeout audit of the regional-streaming change. Earlier verification above remains historical; this follow-up records the fixes and targeted reruns, not a new CPU benchmark or full application E2E acceptance.

findings.issue: Autosave disabled destination browsing and could swallow a click between pointer down and up.
findings.baseline: The App, WorldTravelPanel and bootstrap sources are identical at dba85c8 and 423f710. Rebundling the dba85c8 travel UI in the same controlled session fixture reproduces the lost selection.
findings.fix: Separate browsing from transaction availability: autosave blocks travel submission and its keyboard shortcut, while selecting a destination and closing the panel remain available.
findings.regression: travel-panel.spec.ts holds a real session persistence promise between mouse down and up. It failed on disabled browsing before the fix and passes after the fix.

findings.issue: Simulation generation failure disposed terrain internally and again through the Worker owner; repeated Host closure also closed repositories again.
findings.reproduction: Fault injection during initialization, teleport, boundary crossing and ahead preparation each observed two terrain-dispose calls before the fix.
findings.fix: CombatSimulation and CombatWorkerHost disposal now return immediately when already closed; failure remains fatal.
findings.regression: RegionalStreaming.test.ts covers all four generation-failure paths and disposal during suspended initialization, teleport, crossing and ahead preparation. Each owner closes once; failed or disposed work publishes no partial or late state.

findings.issue: Quiescence requires stopping continuous tick submission; software rendering also exhausted whole-test budgets without a Worker error.
findings.observations: A 120-second fog-drag run timed out in mouse.down after approximately 70 seconds entering wilds and approximately 3.7 seconds per mouse driver round trip. A later 540-second repeated-world run completed all three round trips and their assertions, then timed out before the final refresh.
findings.testChanges: Pause helper preserves an already paused session. Remove redundant drag interpolation while retaining six real drags and the independent 100-event coalescing check. All three save/load round trips remain, through public session.travel; initial entry, final exit and refresh restoration retain UI input.
findings.deadlines: Homestead/fog whole-test budget is 360 seconds and the repeated-world journey is 540 seconds. Each API travel retains a 45-second deadline. UI action/load and production Worker timeout settings are unchanged.
findings.result: All four homestead/fog cases pass across focused runs; the repeated-world case completed in the runner's reported 8.1 minutes.

browser.homesteadAndFog: 3 passed in the expanded rerun; the final repeated-world case passed separately after reducing driver round trips.
browser.productionWorker: 1 passed: real production entry, saved-position initialization and far teleport with complete publications.
browser.startup: 3 passed: graphics failure/retry and disposal during two stalled asset loads.
browser.travelSaveRace: 1 passed: controlled pointer/save interleaving, blocked travel, close/resume and retained selection.

verification.documentation: 37 Markdown files passed; code/design correspondence reviewed.
verification.limitations: Targeted correctness and lifecycle acceptance only. The entire application browser suite was not run, and this does not establish target-device frame rate or remove the previously measured cold-start slice costs.
